title: CS 4535: Reading Bid
description: Due Thu Sep 24, 23:59 ET. Pairs, readings and session dates go up Mon Sep 28.
completedHtml:
Bid recorded.

You can change it any time before Thu Sep 24, 23:59 ET by submitting again. Pairs, readings and session dates go up Mon Sep 28, and off-list proposals are approved or rejected the same day.

elements.name: list_note
elements.html:
The list has thirteen readings and six of them get taught: three sessions, two groups in each. The rest are on the list because a reading you cite in a design doc in November does as much for you as one you presented.

We make the pairing, so rank the readings on what you want to teach, not on what you think is likely to be assigned. The function or learning outcome in brackets is a hint about where to look for your artifact. Any group can take any reading.

elements.name: preferences
elements.title: Rank your top three readings
elements.description: Drag three of the thirteen into the ranked area. First is the one you most want to teach.
elements.selectToRankEmptyRankedAreaText: Drag three readings here, most wanted first.
elements.selectToRankEmptyUnrankedAreaText: No readings left to choose from.

choices.text: R1: An empirical analysis of flaky tests. Luo et al., FSE 2014 (Release and CI)
R2: Usage, costs, and benefits of continuous integration. Hilton et al., ASE 2016 (Release and CI)
R3: Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review. Bacchelli and Bird, ICSE 2013 (LO4)
R4: Modern code review, a case study at Google. Sadowski et al., ICSE-SEIP 2018 (LO4)
R5: Continuous deployment at Facebook and OANDA. Savor et al., ICSE 2016 (Release and CI)
R6: Feature toggles, practitioner practices and a case study. Rahman et al., MSR 2016 (Release and CI)
R7: Why do internet services fail, and what can be done about it? Oppenheimer et al., USITS 2003 (Observability)
R8: Performance anti-patterns in ORM-backed applications. Chen et al., ICSE 2014 (LO2, performance)
R9: Automated detection of accessibility issues with generative AI. He, Huq and Malek, FSE 2025 (Accessibility)
R10: Software documentation issues unveiled. Aghajani et al., ICSE 2019 (Docs and handoff)
R11: Copilot usability and perceived productivity. Vaithilingam, Zhang and Glassman, CHI 2022 EA, with Ziegler et al., CACM 2024 (AI research)
R12: An endless stream of AI slop. Baltes, Cheong and Treude, 2026 (AI research)
R13: The influence of organizational structure on software quality. Nagappan, Murphy and Basili, ICSE 2008 (LO7)

validators.text: Rank exactly three readings, most wanted first.

pages.name: why
pages.title: Why, and what you'd bring
pages.description: One sentence on each of the three. Then the artifact: something from Pawtograder you think you could bring to show the reading applies to us.

elements.name: why_first
elements.title: Your first choice: why that reading?

validators.text: One sentence. Past about 300 characters you're making the case rather than naming the reason.

elements.name: why_second
elements.title: Your second choice: why that reading?

elements.name: why_third
elements.title: Your third choice: why that reading?

elements.name: artifact_first
elements.title: The artifact you think you could bring
elements.description: A PR. A diagram of a subsystem. A measurement you took. A test that fails for the reason the paper predicts. A query that shows the phenomenon in our data. Answer for your first choice, and don't worry about being held to it: you're naming a plausible artifact, not committing to one.

validators.text: Name the thing. "This reminds me of our gradebook" is not an artifact.

pages.name: offlist
pages.title: Proposing a reading that isn't on the list

elements.name: proposing
elements.title: Are you proposing a reading that isn't on the list?
elements.description: Same overall process as the project slate. It has to clear the same two bars the list cleared: it reports evidence, and it applies to Pawtograder. Approved or rejected by Mon Sep 28.

elements.name: proposal_citation
elements.title: The paper, with venue and year

elements.name: proposal_result
elements.title: What it measured, and how big the result was
elements.description: Everything on the list reports evidence, because you're being asked what the result was and how big it was. A position paper gives you nothing to say there.

elements.name: proposal_artifact
elements.title: The artifact you'd bring, in two sentences
elements.description: Every slot has to produce an artifact from our codebase. There are wonderful papers that would leave you with nothing to bring to the room.

validators.text: Two sentences on the artifact, same bar as the on-list question.

elements.name: proposal_over_first
elements.title: Would you take this over the reading you ranked first?
